direct_answer:
Aker BP states that it applies a systematic double materiality assessment (DMA) to identify material impacts, risks and opportunities (IROs) and the associated sustainability matters for reporting, covering both (i) impacts from its activities on environment and society (impact materiality/inside-out) and (ii) financial risks and opportunities sustainability issues pose to its business model and performance (financial materiality/outside-in), including reputational risk and dependencies on natural, human and social resources [Source 1]. The DMA was first conducted in 2023 and revised in 2024 based on new information, implementation guidance and EFRAG’s draft oil & gas sector standard; it included mapping IROs, their dependencies, and their connection to Aker BP’s own operations and value chain [Source 4].

Process-wise, Aker BP describes a four-step DMA considering activities, business relationships and geographies, focusing in own operations on oil and gas production (highest potential for material impact), in the upstream value chain mainly on development projects (significant construction activity), and acknowledging downstream impacts related to the use of petroleum products; it is working with suppliers/partners to improve value chain understanding and update the DMA as new information becomes available [Source 3]. The methodology includes assessing IROs using severity × likelihood ratings aligned with the enterprise risk management approach (consequence × probability) and prioritising/handling them in the same tool as other company risks [Source 1]. The process is described as structured and iterative: defining business context (activities, business model, value chain, stakeholders, boundaries), identifying actual/potential IROs using top-down and bottom-up approaches with internal/external stakeholder input and quantitative sources, assessing and prioritising IROs against impact and financial materiality criteria using a standardised rating system, then validating outcomes by management and the Board and monitoring for updates if circumstances change [Source 9].

Stakeholder engagement is described as open and proactive dialogue to identify risks, opportunities and actual/potential impacts, including public consultations for PDO impact assessments (sent to 40+ stakeholders and published), a whistleblowing channel, and other internal/external channels [Source 2]. Aker BP states it includes stakeholders’ perspectives and priorities in the DMA; in 2024 this was achieved through in-depth interviews and workshops with internal management and subject matter experts, building on prior-year interviews involving owners, key suppliers, customers, NGOs and authorities [Source 2].

Sustainability matters identified as material from both an impact and a financial perspective (i.e., high impact and high financial relevance/strategic highest priority) are: climate change, own workforce, pollution, business conduct, and resource use and circular economy [Source 3].
compliance_rationale: The report evidences that Aker BP conducted a DMA covering both impact and financial materiality, describes key methodological elements (four-step process; severity×likelihood scoring aligned to ERM; consideration of dependencies between impacts and financial risks/opportunities; value chain coverage; validation by management/Board; ongoing monitoring) and describes stakeholder engagement channels and how stakeholder perspectives were incorporated [Source 1] [Source 2] [Source 3] [Source 4] [Source 9]. It also clearly identifies which sustainability matters are material from both perspectives (climate change, own workforce, pollution, business conduct, resource use & circular economy) [Source 3]. However, the retrieved passages do not provide the detailed list of material IROs (Table 3) or explicit qualitative/quantitative thresholds used to determine materiality, limiting full assessment against ESRS 1 Appendix requirements based solely on the provided evidence [Source 7] [Source 9].
disclosure_gaps: Explicit qualitative and/or quantitative thresholds (or cut-offs) used to determine which impacts/risks/opportunities are material (beyond stating a standardised rating system and severity×likelihood approach) [Source 1] [Source 9].
Complete list of material impacts, risks and opportunities (IROs) and their mapping to sustainability matters (Table 3 is referenced but not included in the retrieved passages) [Source 7].

Clear explanation of how impact materiality criteria (e.g., scale, scope, irremediable character) were applied in practice; the passages mention severity×likelihood but do not evidence the sub-components [Source 1] [Source 9].

Clear explanation of how financial materiality magnitude/likelihood were assessed and how material financial effects were determined; the passages note challenges in measuring financial effects but do not evidence the assessment thresholds [Source 7].
Explicit disclosure of interdependencies/cross-matter effects where actions on one matter create material negative impacts/risks in other matters (not evidenced in the retrieved passages) [Source 1].
key_findings: DMA covers both impact (inside-out) and financial (outside-in) materiality, including reputational risk and dependencies on natural, human and social resources [Source 1].
DMA revised in 2024 (initially conducted in 2023) and includes mapping of IROs, dependencies, and links to own operations and value chain [Source 4].

Assessment considers activities, business relationships and geographies; focuses on oil & gas production for own operations, development projects for upstream value chain, and acknowledges downstream impacts from use of petroleum products [Source 3].
IROs are assessed using severity×likelihood ratings aligned with enterprise risk management and prioritised in the same tool as other company risks [Source 1].

Stakeholder engagement informs DMA via multiple channels (PDO impact assessment consultations, whistleblowing, etc.); 2024 DMA used internal interviews/workshops and built on prior-year interviews with owners, suppliers, customers, NGOs and authorities [Source 2].
Sustainability matters identified as material from both impact and financial perspectives: climate change, own workforce, pollution, business conduct, resource use and circular economy [Source 3].
